name: Strait of Malacca
genZNote: Basically every ship going between the Indian Ocean and East Asia funnels through here — it's the busiest strait on Earth by traffic, not by width.

sections.heading: 🚨 Location & What It Connects
bullets: A long strait between the Malay Peninsula (Malaysia) to the north-east and the Indonesian island of Sumatra to the south-west.
Connects the Andaman Sea/Indian Ocean to the South China Sea/Pacific Ocean.
One of the busiest shipping lanes in the world by number of vessel transits, though not the busiest by cargo value at every point along it.

sections.heading: ⚓ Why It Matters
bullets: The main sea route linking the Indian Ocean (and everything beyond it — the Middle East, Europe, East Africa) to East Asia (China, Japan, South Korea).
Singapore sits right at its south-eastern mouth and is one of the world's busiest transshipment ports partly because of this location.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 India Connection
bullets: India's trade with East and Southeast Asia largely moves through the Strait of Malacca, making it strategically important to India's 'Act East' trade and connectivity goals.
India's Andaman & Nicobar Islands sit close to the strait's western approach, giving India a natural vantage point over this route.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The Strait of Malacca, between Malaysia and Sumatra, links the Indian Ocean to the South China Sea and is one of the world's busiest shipping lanes.
keyFacts: Between the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra (Indonesia).
Connects the Indian Ocean (via the Andaman Sea) to the South China Sea/Pacific.
Singapore sits at its south-eastern mouth.
Key route for India's trade with East/Southeast Asia.
commonConfusion: Don't confuse the Strait of Malacca (Indian Ocean ↔ South China Sea) with the Sunda or Lombok Straits — those are alternative, less-used routes further south through Indonesia.

highYieldFacts: Malacca connects Indian Ocean ↔ South China Sea.
Between Malaysia and Sumatra (Indonesia); Singapore at its mouth.
One of the busiest straits in the world by vessel traffic.
commonTraps: A blockage or heavy congestion at Malacca is why alternate routes like the Sunda and Lombok Straits get discussed as backups — know that relationship.
mustRemember: Malacca = Indian Ocean's gateway to East Asia; Singapore's strategic location comes from sitting right at its mouth.
